newsitem.title: USA: Possis submits additional data to FDA.
newsitem.headline: Possis submits additional data to FDA.

text.p: Possis Medical Inc said Tuesday it submitted to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration additional information summarizing the clinical performance of its Perma-Seal Dialysis Access Graft used by kidney dialysis patients.

The FDA is expected within 30 days to review the clinical study data and provide comments that will be incorporated into a complete submission planned for late June or July 1997 seeking marketing approval for the graft, Possis said.
"FDA review of our 510(k) submission and a final decision concerning clearance to market the Perma-Seal Graft in the United States is expected in the fall of 1997," Possis said.

Chief executive Robert Dutcher said, "We are in discussions with several companies as we focus on selecting a new distribution channel for the Perma-Seal Graft. The graft is now saleable in various markets outside the United States and our goal is to finalize new worldwide distribution prior to the receipt of U.S. marketing clearance."
In December, Possis and C.R. Bard Inc terminated a distribution deal for the Perma-Seal.

The Perma-Seal Graft is a synthetic tube designed to be implanted in the arm to connect an artery and a vein. The self-sealing tube can be punctured periodically by a needle connecting the patient to a kidney dialysis machine. The synthetic graft is intended to reduce bleeding, healing and dialysis time for patients who frequently need dialysis.
Shares in Possis were up 1/4 to 13-1/2.
